explanation: Several of Siberia's great rivers flow north. In spring their upper reaches thaw while their mouths are still frozen, so meltwater spills over vast floodplains.

claims.text: The Lena flows north across Siberia into the Laptev Sea, part of the Arctic Ocean.
The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea, the Amur into the Pacific and the Don into the Sea of Azov.
In spring the upper reaches of Siberia's north-flowing rivers thaw while their lower reaches are still frozen, causing widespread floods.
